/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from itertools import product
for assignment in [(1,2),(2,1)]:
    P={(u,i):int(assignment[u]==i) for u in [0,1] for i in [1,2]}
    feasible=[]
    for bits in product([0,1],repeat=4):
        Z=dict(zip([(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2)],bits))
        holds=all(Z[u,i]>=P[u,i] for u in [0,1] for i in [1,2])
        holds &= all(Z[1,i]<=Z[0,i] for i in [1,2])
        holds &= all(Z[1,i]<=P[1,i]-P[0,i]+1 for i in [1,2])
        if holds: feasible.append(Z)
    o=P[0,1]*P[1,2]
    p=[1,1]
    tpi=sum(p)+o+max(p+[o])
    print({'stage_assignment':assignment,'constraints_6_feasible':bool(feasible),'Z_example':feasible[0] if feasible else None,'modeled_communication_cost':o,'modeled_TPI_c2':tpi})
print('ViT EnvB ratio to best baseline:',45.58/38.74)
print('BERT EnvB ratio to best baseline:',10.77/8.95)
print('Swin EnvB ratio:',19.08/13.90)
PY"

strengths: UniAP addresses a useful systems problem: jointly selecting pipeline partitions and layer-specific DP, TP, and FSDP strategies under memory constraints. Its application to ViT and Swin provides clear relevance to computer vision.

Table 2 demonstrates meaningful practical gains. On EnvB, UniAP improves ViT throughput by approximately 1.18× over the strongest reported baseline and Swin throughput by 1.37× over Galvatron. On EnvA, it matches Galvatron’s throughput on three models while substantially reducing search time. These improvements have value independently of universal benchmark superiority.

The evaluation covers five Transformer models and four hardware configurations. The reported 3.59% mean estimation error on selected strategies, restricted-search ablations, and topology-aware BERT case study provide useful diagnostic evidence beyond throughput comparisons.
The manuscript is generally well organized. Hardware specifications, model dimensions, batch sizes, measurement windows, and solver settings are documented, supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The main concern determining Weak Reject is correctness of the stated optimization formulation. Equations (6a–c) enforce contiguity but do not enforce topological stage ordering. For a two-layer chain u→v, assigning u to stage 2 and v to stage 1 satisfies these constraints, yet Equation (4) assigns zero communication cost to the edge. The optimizer can therefore favor assignments that omit required communication. Appendix A proves contiguity, which does not resolve this problem.

The claimed MIQP encoding is incomplete. Equations (3) and (4) contain products of four binary variables when expanded, such as P_ui P_vi S_uk S_vl, rather than merely quadratic terms. Auxiliary-variable reformulations are possible, but the manuscript supplies neither those variables nor their linking constraints. This leaves a central gap between the mathematical description and the reported solver implementation.

GPipe activation-memory accounting is insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 constructs M using micro-batch size b=B/c, while Equation (5) contains no explicit factor accounting for retained activations across c micro-batches. With the stated GPipe schedule and checkpointing disabled, those activations accumulate before backward execution. As written, the formulation appears to underestimate peak memory; the manuscript needs to establish how this is handled before claiming memory feasibility.

The optimality and complexity claims exceed the evidence. Appendix D permits early termination with an optimality gap below 4% and imposes a 60-second limit, but achieved gaps and timeout frequencies are not reported. Treating solver runtime as a constant budget in Section 3.5 does not establish polynomial-time recovery of optimal solutions. The empirical search-time results remain useful, but they do not substantiate the repeated optimal-solution claims.

The experiments do not isolate the proposed joint optimization as the source of improvement. Hierarchical optimization is not inherently suboptimal without identifying the relevant restrictions or lost dependencies. Figure 7 compares joint search against inter-only and intra-only search, rather than a hierarchical planner using the same cost model and execution backend. Since UniAP also reports better cost estimation, the attribution of gains specifically to joint search remains uncertain.

The search-time comparisons require narrower interpretation. The reported metric measures UOP and excludes profiling, while Section 4.1 explicitly attributes substantial acceleration to multithreaded solving versus single-threaded baseline search. These are legitimate system advantages, but matched-resource comparisons and profiling costs are missing, limiting conclusions about algorithmic efficiency and total preparation time.
